original_paper.title: Do Null-Type Mutation Operators Help Prevent Null-Type Faults?
original_paper.audited_claim: Four null-type operators are evaluated against traditional mutation operators using VideoStore and 15 open-source Java projects.

contents_verified: Reports/TypeReports, Reports/SubsumingReports, and project coverage reports
15 matching project versions in both comparator trees

source_report_outcomes.unit: project for per-project type counts; mutant for kill/survival; dynamic subsumption report for redundancy

aggregate.interpretation: These are inspected source-package reports, not outcomes generated in this session. The paper reports null-type mutants as complementary to traditional mutants, with marginally increased redundancy; this audit does not validate that claim independently.

endpoint_tuple.object: Java test suites and null-type fault mutants
endpoint_tuple.intervention: LittleDarwin-Null with NullifyReturnValue, NullifyInputVariable, NullifyObjectInitialization, and NegateNullCheck (reported in package as removeNullCheck)

observed_result_or_blocker.decision: The endpoint and source package are authenticated enough for a future reproduction plan, but the full endpoint-matched experiment is not locally executable in this session.
blockers: No usable Java runtime: both java and javac fail before execution.
No Maven, Ant, or Gradle executable is available for the heterogeneous project builds.
The bundled LittleDarwin driver is Python-2 syntax, while the available python command is Python 3; no Python-2 interpreter is available.
The projects use legacy build/dependency contracts, including Java source/target 1.5 in inspected POM/build files, so a current unpinned toolchain would not be an endpoint-preserving substitute.
A package containing precomputed reports is not a substitute for rerunning the source-pinned mutation/test oracle.
observed_result_or_blocker.not_claimed: No claim is made that null-type operators are ineffective, effective, or independently reproduced; the reported counts remain source-package observations only.

uncertainty: The archive is pinned by URL, byte count, and SHA-256, but it does not provide a modern VCS commit identifier for every bundled project/tool component.
The paper and package report dynamic subsumption, whose accuracy depends on the available test suite; this audit did not recompute it.
The exact original environment versions, dependency-cache state, and run order are not fully specified by the inspected materials.
The aggregate source reports include generated artifacts; their presence does not establish that the bundled source can still reproduce them.
The local no-go is an environment/toolchain feasibility result, not a scientific null result.

next_falsifiable_action.action: Provision an isolated, version-recorded legacy toolchain containing a usable JDK compatible with the projects' Java 1.5-era builds, Maven/Ant as required by each project, and Python 2.7 or a separately validated port of LittleDarwin; then run one fixed project (JSQLParser 0.9.4) from clean Traditional and NullType trees before expanding to all 15.
next_falsifiable_action.enabling_condition: Do not proceed until java -version, javac -version, the project build/test command, and LittleDarwin-Null produce successful, independently inspectable outputs on that single project with exact surviving/killed denominators and a reproducible report hash.
next_falsifiable_action.falsification: If the clean single-project smoke cannot compile, run the source test suite, generate both operator groups, and emit the package-compatible kill/subsumption records under the pinned environment, terminate the reproduction attempt and retain the no-go.
